newsitem.title: GERMANY: China, U.S. seen leading rise in 96/97 soymeal use.
newsitem.headline: China, U.S. seen leading rise in 96/97 soymeal use.

text.p: Global soybean meal consumption in 1996/97 (Oct/Sept) is forecast at 90.20 million tonnes, compared with 87.74 million in 1995/96, the independent Oil World newsletter said on Tuesday.
It predicted a sharp jump in soymeal use in China and a modest rise in the U.S.
China's consumption was put at 9.13 million tonnes after 6.36 million in the previous season, while the U.S. were seen consuming 24.60 million tonnes after 24.12 million previously.
Higher demand was likely to counter the effects of historically high soymeal prices and high premiums over other oilmeals and grains, Oil World said.
Lower soymeal prices would result in even more imports.
Prices were likely to fall under pressure from Latin American new crop supplies.
European Union imports of soymeal would fall to 10.40 million this season, compared with the 10.66 million expected a month ago and 12.59 million in 1995/96, Oil World added.
Soymeal use in the EU was forecast at 21.5 million tonnes versus the 21.8 million expected a month ago and 12.6 million in 1995/96.
The EU derives meal from direct imports and local crushing.
